project.name: IT Systems Inventory and Lifecycle Management
project.problem_statement: The company has many overlapping IT systems with different costs, risks, and lifecycle states. IT Business Owners and related stakeholders lack a single system for inventory, planning, deprecation, cost management, and risk oversight.
project.system_scope: Web-based inventory and lifecycle management system for all non-OT IT systems.

business_goals: Improve planning of IT system purchasing and lifecycle decisions.
Create a single inventory source of truth for non-OT IT systems.
Improve visibility of overlap, cost, risk, and deprecation status.
success_criteria: Stakeholders can inventory all non-OT systems in one place.
Lifecycle and approval states are visible and configurable.
Downstream systems can consume data through an API.
The system supports lifecycle planning, deprecation, and cost/risk management workflows.

actors.name: IT Business Owner
actors.description: Owns business accountability for systems and uses the platform for inventory, planning, lifecycle oversight, and approvals.

actors.name: Technical Owner
actors.description: Maintains technical metadata, lifecycle details, and system-level attributes.

actors.name: Enterprise Architect
actors.description: Reviews overlap, portfolio fit, capability coverage, and strategic lifecycle direction.

actors.name: Procurement/Security/Finance/Application Owner
actors.description: Contributes governance, cost, security, and ownership review activities.

actors.name: Downstream API Consumer
actors.description: Reads inventory and lifecycle data through the API for reporting or automation.

use_cases.name: Register a system
use_cases.goal: Add a non-OT IT system to the inventory.
main_success_scenario: IT Business Owner opens the registration flow.
User enters required metadata for the system.
System validates the submission.
System creates the inventory record.
extensions: A potential duplicate system is detected.

use_cases.name: Edit system metadata
use_cases.goal: Maintain and update metadata for an existing system.
main_success_scenario: Technical Owner locates the system record.
Technical Owner edits metadata fields.
System validates the changes.
System saves the updated record and audit trail.
extensions: User lacks permission to edit certain fields.
A field value violates policy or data validation.

use_cases.name: Compare overlapping systems
use_cases.goal: Identify and compare systems with overlapping purpose or capability.
main_success_scenario: Enterprise Architect searches or selects systems for comparison.
System displays metadata, capabilities, cost, risk, and lifecycle information side by side.
Enterprise Architect reviews overlap indicators and redundancy signals.
System supports documenting comparison outcomes.
extensions: Overlap signals are incomplete because metadata is missing.
Comparison scope spans too many systems and must be narrowed.

use_cases.name: Track lifecycle state
use_cases.goal: Maintain lifecycle state and progression for a system.
main_success_scenario: IT Business Owner opens the lifecycle view for a system.
User reviews current lifecycle state and allowed transitions.
User updates or submits a lifecycle transition.
System records the transition and exposes the updated state.
extensions: Requested transition is not allowed by workflow rules.

use_cases.name: Review risks and costs
use_cases.goal: Inspect risk and cost dimensions for a system or portfolio slice.
main_success_scenario: Governance user opens a system or portfolio view.
System shows annual cost, contract end, owner gap, security rating, business criticality, technical debt, and redundancy.
Governance user filters or searches the results.
Governance user records or exports the review outcome.
extensions: Required source data is missing or stale.
Some data is restricted by role.

use_cases.name: Approve deprecation and stage gates
use_cases.goal: Execute workflow approvals for lifecycle stage gates and deprecation decisions.
main_success_scenario: A lifecycle or deprecation request is submitted.
Governance user reviews the request and supporting metadata.
Governance user approves or rejects the stage-gate decision.
System records the decision and updates the workflow state.
extensions: A rejection sends the item back for rework.

use_cases.name: Report portfolio gaps
use_cases.goal: Identify gaps, duplication, or planning issues across the IT system portfolio.
main_success_scenario: Enterprise Architect selects a scope such as capability, geography, or ownership area.
System analyzes the selected inventory subset.
System presents detected gaps, duplication, or lifecycle concerns.
Enterprise Architect exports or shares the results.
extensions: The selected data set is incomplete.
Gap analysis rules need refinement for the selected scope.

use_cases.name: Expose inventory data by API
use_cases.goal: Retrieve inventory and lifecycle data programmatically.
main_success_scenario: Downstream system authenticates to the API.
Downstream system requests inventory or lifecycle data.
System validates access rights and query parameters.
System returns the requested data.

functional: The system must manage inventory for all non-OT IT systems.
The system must allow users to register a system.
The system must allow authorized users to edit system metadata.
The system must support comparison of overlapping systems.
The system must track configurable lifecycle states, including proposed, active, tolerated, sunset, and decommissioned.
The system must track annual cost, contract end, owner gap, security rating, business criticality, technical debt, and redundancy.
The system must support business workflows such as stage gates and approval states.
The system must provide API access for downstream systems and AI agents.
The system must support reporting of portfolio gaps.
The system must support risk and cost review across inventoried systems.
non_functional: The UI must be web based.
The system must support role-based access control.
The system must provide an audit trail.
The system must support search and filtering.
The system must provide availability of at least 99%.
The system must provide acceptable web performance for normal page rendering.

assumptions: The system acts as the CMDB for IT applications and systems, excluding OT systems.
API consumers include downstream reporting systems and AI agents.
Lifecycle states are configurable even though an initial default set exists.
V1 includes workflow support for approvals and stage gates, not just passive inventory.
The UCP inputs were estimated using defaults for a similar internal enterprise system at a company of about 1000 people.
open_questions: Did performance mean page rendering should be less than 1 second rather than greater than 1 second?
Are integrations/interfaces first-class inventory objects or only metadata on systems?
Should procurement, security, finance, and application owners have distinct roles and workflows in V1?
What exact approval workflows and stage-gate states are required in V1?
What data model is required for overlap analysis and portfolio gap reporting?
